list.title: Plugin marketplace
list.description: The marketplace every workspace draws from, retired rows included. Workspace owners add these plugins to their workspace; members connect them with their own accounts. Private plugins a workspace creates for itself are not listed here.
list.brokenHeading: {count, plural, one {# row cannot} other {# rows cannot}} complete an OAuth connect.
list.brokenDetail: {labels} — marked pre-registered with no client id, so the consent screen is built with an empty client_id and the provider refuses it. Open the row and set the client id.
list.filterAria: Filter the catalog by whether a row is active
list.searchPlaceholder: Search by label, key or provider

error.title: The plugin catalog could not be loaded.
error.body: Check the assistant service, and that your session still holds the platform admin role.

list.emptyCatalog: The catalog is empty. Nothing is on offer in WarpBot, for anyone.
list.missingClientIdExplanation: This row is marked pre-registered but holds no OAuth client id, so a connect attempt builds a consent URL with an empty client_id and the provider refuses it. Set the client id below.
list.workspaceCount: {count, plural, =0 {no workspaces} one {# workspace} other {# workspaces}}
list.footerNote: Workspaces: those whose list holds the plugin, plus those that never edited their list and whose members already use it. Installed by: members who have it installed now. A native row is served by compiled-in code and takes its OAuth client from service configuration, not from the catalog — so this screen can neither set nor vouch for one.

dialog.title: Add an MCP app
dialog.intro: The row appears in every user's plugin list as soon as it is saved — no deploy and no restart. It is created as an MCP row that takes its key as its OAuth provider, with no tools: those arrive from the server's own tools/list on the first connect, and can be written by hand from the row's page.

description.label: Description
description.hint: What a user reads in the catalog before installing it.

pluginKey.label: Plugin key
pluginKey.hint: Lower-case, and permanent: it is this row's URL and its OAuth provider name. Reserved: {keys}.

mcpServerUrl.label: MCP server URL
mcpServerUrl.hint: Absolute https://. The tokens this row carries travel over it, so http is refused — on localhost too.

avatarUrl.label: Avatar URL
avatarUrl.hint: Optional. An http(s) URL or a site-relative path.

requiredScopes.label: Required scopes
requiredScopes.hint: Optional, one per line. Most MCP servers advertise their own on connect.

authMode.oauthNote: Users sign in on the provider's page. Recommended when the server supports it.
authMode.apiKeyTitle: Each user pastes an API key
authMode.apiKeyNote: No OAuth. The key is checked against the server, stored encrypted, and sent as a Bearer token.

oauth.checkboxTitle: This server needs a hand-registered OAuth client
oauth.checkboxBody: Leave this off unless you know it does. The registration ladder runs on the first connect and picks Client ID Metadata Documents or dynamic registration on its own; supplying a client id here instead marks the row preregistered, which is the state that must always hold an id.

clientSecret.label: Client secret
clientSecret.hint: Optional — leave blank for a public client. It goes in and does not come back: no endpoint ever returns it, and it can only be replaced or cleared from the row's page afterwards.

authorizationEndpoint.label: Authorization endpoint
authorizationEndpoint.hint: Optional. Blank lets discovery find it.

dialog.catalogNotLoadedNote: The catalog has not loaded, so a key already taken by another row cannot be caught here — the server will still refuse it.

toast.problemCount: {count, plural, one {# field still needs} other {# fields still need}} fixing. Nothing was sent.
toast.success: {key} added to the catalog. It is live for every user immediately — no deploy.
toast.errorFallback: Could not add the plugin to the catalog.

notFound.title: No such plugin
notFound.body: Nothing in the catalog is keyed {key}. It may have been hard-deleted.

loadError.title: This plugin could not be loaded
loadError.fallback: The assistant service did not answer.

cannotConnectBanner.title: This row cannot complete an OAuth connect.
cannotConnectBanner.body: This row is marked pre-registered but holds no OAuth client id, so a connect attempt builds a consent URL with an empty client_id and the provider refuses it. Set the client id below.

toast.rediscoverSuccess: Discovery cleared. The registration ladder runs again on the next connect.
toast.rediscoverFail: Could not clear discovery for this plugin.

metadata.heading: Catalog entry
metadata.unsavedChanges: {count, plural, one {# unsaved change} other {# unsaved changes}}
metadata.label: Label

avatarUrl.label: Avatar URL
avatarUrl.hint: An http(s) URL or a site-relative path beginning with /. Empty clears it.

sortOrder.label: Sort order
sortOrder.hint: The curated order the catalog renders. Ties break on label.

mcpServerUrl.label: MCP server URL
mcpServerUrl.hint: An absolute https:// URL. It cannot be cleared on an MCP row.

metadata.nativeNote: A native row is served by compiled-in code, which never reads an MCP server URL — so the field is not offered here. The server would refuse it anyway.

requiredScopes.label: Required scopes
requiredScopes.hint: One per line. Repeats are dropped by the server.

authMode.heading: How users connect
authMode.descriptionApiKey: Each user pastes their own API key. WarpTalk checks it against the server, stores it encrypted and sends it as a Bearer token.
authMode.descriptionOAuth: Users sign in on the provider's own page. The OAuth client below is resolved on the first connect.
authMode.confirmWarning: Every user connected to {label} will have to connect again.

toast.switchedToApiKey: Users now connect with their own API key. Existing connections were ended.
toast.switchedToOAuth: Users now sign in with OAuth. Existing connections were ended.
toast.switchFail: Could not change how users connect.

oauth.heading: OAuth client

sourceNotes.unresolved: Discovery has not run. The registration ladder chooses on the first connect.
sourceNotes.preregistered: An operator supplied the client id. It must be present on this row.
sourceNotes.cimd: The client is identified by our published metadata document URL.
sourceNotes.dcr: Credentials came from RFC 7591 dynamic registration.
sourceNotes.api_key: No OAuth. Each user pastes their own API key, sent to the server as a Bearer token.

native.title: This plugin's OAuth client is not in the catalog.
native.body: A native row is served by compiled-in code that reads its client id and secret from service configuration. The server refuses to write them here, and offering the form anyway would let someone chasing an empty client_id type one in, watch it save, and believe the problem fixed while nothing had changed. Set it in the environment the assistant service runs with instead.

clientId.label: Client id
clientId.hint: Saving marks this row pre-registered. A client id is public by construction — it travels in every authorization URL the browser follows.

secretMode.leaveUnset: Leave it unset — this row has no secret

oauth.secretHint: A secret goes in and does not come back. Nothing on this screen can show you the stored one, so "keep" is the default: rotating an id must not wipe a secret merely because the field beneath it was blank.

authorizationEndpoint.label: Authorization endpoint
authorizationEndpoint.hint: Optional. Blank leaves whatever discovery cached.

oauth.dirtyCount: {count, plural, one {# field differs} other {# fields differ}} from the stored row.

toast.clientIdRequired: A client id is required. Clearing one is not something this endpoint does.
toast.secretRequired: Type the new client secret, or choose to keep or clear the stored one.
toast.savedCleared: OAuth client saved and the stored secret cleared.
toast.savedKept: OAuth client saved. The stored secret was left alone.
toast.saveFail: Could not save the OAuth client.

tools.heading: Tool manifest
tools.neverConfirmed: hand-authored — never confirmed by a tools/list
tools.intro: The whole manifest, replaced in one write. pluginKey is stamped from the route and must not appear here. Saving clears the tools_synced_at marker, because a hand edit is not a successful tools/list and should not look like one.
tools.storedCount: {count, plural, one {# tool} other {# tools}} stored

toast.problems: The manifest has {count, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}}. Nothing was sent.
toast.replacedEmpty: Manifest replaced. This plugin now advertises no tools.
toast.replacedCount: Manifest replaced — {count, plural, one {# tool} other {# tools}}.
toast.replaceFail: Could not replace the tool manifest.

audits.heading: Tool calls
audits.filterPlaceholder: Filter by outcome, e.g. success or missing_scope
audits.filterAria: Filter recorded tool calls by outcome

error.title: The tool-call record could not be loaded.

audits.emptyFiltered: No recorded call matches that outcome.
audits.emptyAll: Nothing has called a tool on this plugin yet.

danger.heading: Delete
danger.title: Remove this row from the catalog entirely.
danger.referencedBody: Refused while anything references it — {installs, plural, one {# installation} other {# installations}} and {connections, plural, one {# connection} other {# connections}} still do. Retire it instead: a retired row is hidden from every catalog while those references stay intact.
danger.notReferencedBody: Nothing references this row, so it can be deleted outright. Retiring it is still the reversible option.

dialog.title: Delete {label}?
dialog.description: {key} will be removed from the catalog along with its tool manifest and any stored OAuth client. Its recorded tool calls are not deleted. This cannot be undone from this screen.

toast.inUseFail: This plugin is still referenced and cannot be hard-deleted.

footer.prefix: Edits are stamped with the account that made them.
footer.noRecordedEditor: This row has no recorded editor — it was last written by a migration, or by a token carrying no usable subject. Created {date}.
